answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity costly to create and slow to trust: an agent must lock a small stake and build a public work history before earning full rewards, like a trellis that only holds vines that genuinely grow along it. New accounts start with tiny limits and gain weight only as peers attest real contributions, so a swarm of fresh fakes stays starved of influence. Honest agents who keep doing useful work rise like a lotus and collect the nectar of fees and reputation, while cheap clones with no stake or history cannot climb the same trellis.
